name: Bhāskararāya
summary: The great 18th-c. systematizer of Śrīvidyā (initiatory name Bhāsurānandanātha), disciple of Nṛsiṃhānandanātha: author of the Saubhāgyabhāskara on the Lalitā Sahasranāma, the Setubandha on the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, the Varivasyārahasya, the Guptavatī on the Devī Māhātmya and commentaries on the Tripurā, Bhāvanā and Kaula Upaniṣads; he read the Śākta tantras through Mīmāṃsā and Vedānta and defended their Vedic standing.
places: the Kāverī region of Tamil Nadu (by tradition, a village named after him)

realization_account.text: Remembered as a perfected upāsaka of Lalitā who performed great sacrifices and vanquished opponents in debate at Kāśī; his life is told in the Bhāskaravilāsa.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Initiatory name and guru's name checked in the Varivasyārahasya colophon and the Saubhāgyabhāskara opening. Places and exact dates are from memory (low).

name: Nṛsiṃhānandanātha
summary: Bhāskararāya's guru, praised at the opening of the Saubhāgyabhāskara and the Varivasyārahasya as the teacher of the vidyās and mantras.

name: Umānandanātha
summary: Disciple of Bhāskararāya, author of the Nityotsava, the standard manual expanding the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra.

name: Puṇyānanda
summary: A paramahaṃsa teacher of Śrīvidyā, author of the Kāmakalāvilāsa and guru of Amṛtānanda (as the Dīpikā's colophons state).

name: Amṛtānanda
summary: Disciple of Puṇyānanda, author of the Dīpikā on the Yoginīhṛdaya (and, by tradition, the Saubhāgyasudhodaya); he explains Tripurā as the fusion of light and self-awareness.

name: Naṭanānandanātha
summary: Commentator on the Kāmakalāvilāsa (Cidvallī).

name: Lakṣmīdhara (Lolla Lakṣmīdhara)
summary: Commentator on the Saundaryalaharī (the Lakṣmīdharā) and on the Subhagodaya; the classical exponent of the Samaya school, who restricts worship to the inner space, teaches the fivefold equality of Śiva and Śakti, and rejects the sixty-four tantras and Kaula practice as outside the Vedic path.

scholarly.text: c. early 16th c. CE; associated with the court of Pratāparudra Gajapati of Orissa

notes: Distinct from Lakṣmīdhara Bhaṭṭa, author of the Kṛtyakalpataru (tch:laksmidhara in U02/U07), and from Lakṣmīdhara Kavi of the Advaitamakaranda (tch:laksmidhara-kavi), though some identify him with the latter. U08 attached the Saundaryalaharī commentary to tch:laksmidhara — needs deduplication.

name: Kaivalyāśrama
summary: A renunciant commentator on the Saundaryalaharī (Saubhāgyavardhinī).

name: Kāmeśvarasūri
summary: Commentator on the Saundaryalaharī (Aruṇāmodinī), as remembered here.

name: Subhagānandanātha
summary: Author of the Manoramā commentary on the Tantrarāja up to paṭala 22; styled in its colophons 'Prapañcasāra-siṃharāja-prakāśa'.

name: Prakāśānanda Deśika
summary: Disciple of Subhagānandanātha who completed the Manoramā on the last fourteen paṭalas of the Tantrarāja at his teacher's command. Not the Advaitin Prakāśānanda.

name: Śivānanda (author of the Ṛjuvimarśinī)
summary: Commentator on the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava (Ṛjuvimarśinī). Not the 20th-c. Swami Sivananda.

name: Vidyānanda (author of the Artharatnāvalī)
summary: Commentator on the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava (Artharatnāvalī).

name: Vidyāraṇya Yati (author of the Śrīvidyārṇava)
summary: The renunciant to whom the Śrīvidyārṇava Tantra is ascribed; tradition sometimes identifies him with Mādhava Vidyāraṇya of Śṛṅgeri (tch:vidyaranya), which scholars doubt.

name: Nāgabhaṭṭa
summary: Compiler of the Tripurāsārasamuccaya.

name: Rāmeśvara (commentator on the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra)
summary: Author of the Saubhāgyodaya commentary on the Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra (usually dated 1831).

name: Laghubhaṭṭāraka
summary: Kashmiri author to whom the Laghustava (Laghustuti) to Tripurā is ascribed.

name: The eight Vāgdevatās (Vaśinī and the others)
summary: The eight goddesses of speech — Vaśinī, Kāmeśvarī, Modinī, Vimalā, Aruṇā, Jayinī, Sarveśvarī and Kaulinī — who composed the Lalitā Sahasranāma at the Goddess's command and preside over the eight-cornered enclosure of the Śrīcakra; the Saundaryalaharī (17) makes them givers of poetic speech.

name: Paraśurāma (Jāmadagnya Bhārgava)
summary: The avatāra-sage, son of Jamadagni and Reṇukā, who in the Śrīvidyā tradition is the chief disciple of Mahādeva and author of the Kalpasūtra, and who in the Tripurā Rahasya receives the teaching of Tripurā from Dattātreya.
notes: PKS colophon (10.85) names Paraśurāma, chief disciple of Mahādeva (checked).

name: Manmatha (Kāma)
summary: The god of love, one of the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā; the Kādi form of the vidyā is called after him (Kāmarāja-vidyā). In the Lalitopākhyāna he is burned by Śiva and revived by Lalitā.

name: Mūka Kavi
summary: The 'mute poet' of Kāñcī who by tradition received speech through Kāmākṣī's grace and poured out the Mūka Pañcaśatī; the Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi tradition counts him among its ācāryas.

realization_account.text: Mute from birth, he became a poet when the Goddess (or a devotee in her presence) gave him her grace.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Abhirāmi Paṭṭar
summary: 18th-c. Tamil devotee of the Goddess Abhirāmi of Tirukkaṭavūr and author of the Abhirāmi Antāti.

realization_account.text: Absorbed in the Goddess, he told the king that the day was full moon; to vindicate him the Goddess threw her earring into the sky, which shone as the moon.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar
summary: Karnatic composer and Śrīvidyā initiate whose Kamalāmbā Navāvaraṇa songs set the Śrīcakra worship to music.
notes: His initiation into Śrīvidyā by a yogin at Kāśī is the tradition's account (not detailed here).

name: Śyāmā Śāstrī
summary: Karnatic composer of Tañjāvūr devoted to the Goddess Kāmākṣī (Bangāru Kāmākṣī), whose songs are addressed almost entirely to her.

name: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita
summary: 17th-c. poet and minister at Madurai, grand-nephew of Appayya Dīkṣita, author of the Ānandasāgarastava to Mīnākṣī.

name: Kālidāsa
summary: The classical poet; Śākta tradition holds that he gained his genius by the Goddess's (Kālī's) grace and ascribes to him the Śyāmalā Daṇḍaka and other hymns.

realization_account.text: An unlettered man who became the greatest poet when the Goddess wrote on his tongue.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: U23 records only the Śākta attributions and legend.

name: Bhairavī Brāhmaṇī
summary: The woman tantric adept who guided Ramakrishna through the practices of the sixty-four tantras at Dakṣiṇeśvar.

name: Amṛtānandanātha Sarasvatī (of Devīpuram)
summary: 20th-c. Śrīvidyā teacher who founded the Devīpuram temple in Andhra with a walk-in Śrī Meru, and taught Śrīvidyā worship widely, including to women and non-Brahmins.

name: Śaṅkara
summary: U23 contribution: in the Śrīvidyā tradition's account Śaṅkara is the author of the Saundaryalaharī, the Triśatī-bhāṣya and hymns to the Goddess, an upāsaka of Śrīvidyā in the line of Gauḍapāda, and the one who installed Śrīcakras at Śṛṅgeri (Śāradā) and Kāñcī (Kāmākṣī) and placed Śrīcakras in the earrings of Akhilāṇḍeśvarī at Tiruvāṉaikkā; scholars doubt the ascriptions.

name: Gauḍapāda
summary: U23 contribution: Śrīvidyā tradition ascribes to him the Subhagodaya and the Śrīvidyāratnasūtra and places him at the head of the line Gauḍapāda - Govinda - Śaṅkara as upāsakas of the Goddess.

name: Hayagrīva
summary: U23 contribution: the teacher of Agastya who reveals the Lalitā Sahasranāma and the Triśatī.

name: Agastya
summary: U23 contribution: one of the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā; the disciple of Hayagrīva to whom the Lalitā Sahasranāma and Triśatī are taught; husband of Lopāmudrā.

name: Lopāmudrā
summary: U23 contribution: one of the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā; the Hādi form of the vidyā is called after her (Lopāmudrā-vidyā).

name: Durvāsas
summary: U23 contribution: identified by the Śrīvidyā tradition with Krodhabhaṭṭāraka, the twelfth of the great worshippers of the vidyā; ascribed the Lalitāstavaratna (Āryādviśatī) and the Śaktimahimnastotra; Bhāskararāya quotes him.

name: Dattātreya
summary: U23 contribution: in the Tripurā Rahasya he teaches Paraśurāma the knowledge and worship of Tripurā; Śrīvidyā tradition links the Kalpasūtra to his teaching.

name: Haritāyana
summary: U23 contribution: the narrator of the Tripurā Rahasya, called Sumedhas, who received the teaching through Paraśurāma.

name: Jayaratha
summary: U23 contribution: author of the Vivaraṇa on the Vāmakeśvarīmata, the Kashmiri commentary on the root Śrīvidyā tantra.

name: Śiva
summary: U23 contribution: as Bhairava / Parameśvara he reveals the Śrīvidyā tantras to the Goddess (Vāmakeśvara, Yoginīhṛdaya, Tantrarāja, Jñānārṇava); as Kāmeśvara he is Lalitā's consort; he is one of the twelve great worshippers of the vidyā.

name: Indra
summary: U23 contribution: one of the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā.

name: Skanda
summary: U23 contribution: one of the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā.

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: U23 contribution: named by Lakṣmīdhara as author of one of the five Śubhāgamas that teach the Vedic Samaya way.

name: Sanaka
summary: U23 contribution: named by Lakṣmīdhara as author of one of the five Śubhāgamas that teach the Vedic Samaya way.

name: Śuka
summary: U23 contribution: named by Lakṣmīdhara as author of one of the five Śubhāgamas that teach the Vedic Samaya way.

name: Sanandana
summary: U23 contribution: named by Lakṣmīdhara as author of one of the five Śubhāgamas that teach the Vedic Samaya way.

name: Sanatkumāra
summary: U23 contribution: named by Lakṣmīdhara as author of one of the five Śubhāgamas that teach the Vedic Samaya way.

name: Ramakrishna
summary: U23 contribution: priest of Kālī at Dakṣiṇeśvar who practised the tantric disciplines under the Bhairavī Brāhmaṇī and worshipped his wife Sāradā as the Goddess Ṣoḍaśī.

name: Maheśvarānanda
summary: U23 contribution: his Mahārthamañjarī and its commentary show the Krama teaching of the Cola country interwoven with Śrīvidyā worship.
